events.objective: Establish the true onset time and blast radius of the incident from telemetry, using 2026-04-02T12:00-14:00 window: (1) per-service error rate, latency (p50/p95/p99), throughput and timeout/retry counts for payment-service and its dependencies — look specifically for HTTP 200 responses with erroneous/degraded business status codes, long-tail latency without 5xx, and reduced request volume; (2) identify any other service whose metrics deviate in the same minute. Report whether the green payment-service HTTP error panel is a real signal or a metric blind spot, and which services show genuine anomalies.

Build the change/context timeline for 2026-04-02 11:00-14:00: list deployments and config changes for payment-service AND all upstream/downstream services and shared components (queues, DB, auth, bank/PSP connectors, feature flags, rate limits), plus the service dependency map for payment-service (who it calls, who calls it, shared components). Also search historical incidents for payment failures where the payment-service error-rate dashboard stayed green. Report what changed and when, which components are shared with other services, and any precedent fitting this signature.

Using the onset time and affected-service set found in task a, correlate them against the change timeline from task b: determine whether any deploy/config change precedes the onset by a plausible interval on the affected components (not only on payment-service), and whether changes are isolated to payment-service or shared. Conclude with the most likely fault location (payment-service, a specific dependency, or external bank side) and rule in/out the client-app/bank-only theory.

events.answer: In 2026-04-02 11:00-14:00 there were zero deployments and exactly one config change: payment-service's bank.api.timeout_ms raised 3000→5000 ms at 11:20:00Z (author p.nair, reason \"partner advisory\"). The only deployment that day was settlement-service v1.9.0 at 10:30 (batch CSV exporter, still live). payment-service calls ledger-db (shared, also used by order/portfolio/settlement-service), bank-partner-api (external, NO telemetry) and kafka (shared); it is called by api-gateway. Given the silent-failure signature, the untraced external bank connector and the shared ledger-db/kafka (usable by neighbours) are the components to inspect; HIST-105 (bank partner API 5xx) is the closest precedent, though no historical incident actually matches 'payment failures with a green error-rate dashboard'.

events.statement: payment-service HTTP error_rate (5xx) stayed flat and normal across the whole window, staying between ~0.16% and ~0.32% (mean 0.22, max 0.32) with no step at 12:15 — the 'green' panel reflects only HTTP 5xx.

payment_success_rate collapsed from ~99% to ~2.5% in one minute: 12:14 = 99.68%, 12:15 = 2.18%, and stayed depressed for the rest of the window (12:52 = 2.14%). This is the true onset — the business-success metric broke exactly at 12:15:00Z while error_rate did not move.

The first error in logs is 12:15:27Z 'payment 45f233b6 marked PENDING_RETRY: mTLS handshake with bank-partner-api rejected'; the diagnosing line appears at 12:16:44Z: 'remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert 45); our client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z'. The cert expiry timestamp equals the onset minute.

Error volume is large and sustained: 313 matched ERROR/WARN log lines for payment-service (311 ERROR) from 12:04:22Z to 13:58:39Z; dominant patterns are 'bank-partner-api call failed: ... tls: expired certificate' (171) and 'marked PENDING_RETRY: mTLS handshake with bank-partner-api rejected' (140).

bank_api_error_rate jumped from 0.2% (12:00) to 12.68% avg/max 100% (12:08) to a sustained 100% from 12:16 onward, confirming all calls to the external bank dependency failed after cert expiry; request_rate stayed flat (~90-110 req/s) so traffic was not reduced.

payment-service latency p99 DROPPED (not rose) after onset: 316-341ms before 12:15, then ~135-147ms for the rest of the window — consistent with calls failing fast at the TLS handshake rather than hanging, so a latency-based alert would also have missed this.

events.answer: The payment-service HTTP error-rate panel is a genuine metric blind spot: HTTP error_rate stayed flat at ~0.2% (5xx only) all window, while the business-level payment_success_rate collapsed from ~99% to ~2.5% at 12:15:00Z and stayed there. events.title: Expired mTLS client certificate to bank-partner-api
Shared dependency (ledger-db / kafka / shared component) failure

events.summary:
H1 (expired mTLS client cert to bank-partner-api) is the best-supported hypothesis: the true onset is tightly established at 2026-04-02T12:15:00Z (payment_success_rate 99.68%->2.18% in one minute), the diagnostic error text names OUR client cert (CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal) with notAfter exactly equal to the onset minute, 171 'tls: expired certificate' errors, bank_api_error_rate sustained 100%, and the fast-fail latency drop (330ms->140ms) explains why the HTTP 5xx panel stayed green. Alternatives H3/H4/H5 are properly contradicted (mis-timed changes, wrong failure mode, wrong layer). However, two things block an "accept": (1) H2 is ranked active at 0.15 but is NOT actually separated from H1 by evidence — both rest on the same client-side error text, and the only discriminator (is the cert internally issued/managed vs partner-provisioned/trust-changed?) has never been queried. (2) H4 was 'rejected' partly by asserting shared-component health without ever querying ledger-db/kafka metrics, and the blast-radius check across neighbours (api-gateway, order/portfolio/settlement) is unanswered — so "fault confined to payment-service's bank path" is inferred from absence of evidence rather than measured. These are obtainable and would change ranking/trust, so send back one targeted round.

Grounding: H1's chain is well grounded on F8/F9/F10/F11/F12/F18. Its two assumptions (internal cert ownership; expiry inferred only from error text) are acknowledged and are exactly the H1-vs-H2 discriminator, which is currently unresolved. H2 cites only UNVERIFIED F6 and has an unevidenced hop — but F9's "our client cert ... notAfter=..." attributed to the client side is the only evidence against it, and since bank-partner-api has no telemetry, the external view is permanently unobtainable; this may be inherently unresolvable rather than fixable.

Temporal: onset is excellently established and the proposed cause (notAfter=12:15:00Z, first rejection 12:15:27Z) precedes it by <1 min — no complaint here.

Scope: only payment-service is examined. No other service's metrics were checked at 12:15; "confined to payment-service" is an unverified claim.

Alternatives: H3/H4/H5 dismissals are sound for timing/failure-mode reasons. H4's rejection is the weakest — it relies on "no change event touches shared components," but the actual test (LEDGER-db/kafka health around 12:15, and non-bank payment paths) was never run, and a shared-component problem could also leave the bank TLS path failing if the cert is unrelated. Worth one confirming query.

Data quality: F7 (green panel) rests on 5xx alone — correctly identified as a blind spot, and F8 provides the business metric. F12 latency drop is a single strong signal, not a lone "healthy" claim. Main gap is the unqueried shared-component/neighbour telemetry and the missing cert-ownership record.

Calibration: 0.78 is too high while H2 remains unevidenced-but-not-separated and blast radius is unchecked. Cap 0.65.

events.answer: The available records confirm the CA/credential ownership indirectly but not directly: no certificate/credential registry, secret-store entry, or renewal record for CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal was retrievable — the only internal discriminator present is HIST-106, our own prior credential_expiry incident with the resolution "Issued new cert; added expiry alert" executed by our team, and the absence of any deploy/config/rotation attempt in 12:15-14:00Z. This pattern supports the cert being an org-owned mTLS client credential whose expiry (not a bank-side trust change) is the mechanism, aligning with H1; but because no verbatim registry/ownership record exists, H2 cannot be fully excluded on the certificate record alone.

events.summary: Round-1 blockers are resolved to the extent obtainable. (1) H1-vs-H2 separation: the shared-component/neighbour telemetry was actually queried, and the discriminator for H2 was pursued to its limit. F23 establishes the credential-use direction is outbound-only (bank-partner-api has no callers, shared=false, no push path), and F19/F20/F24 establish the closest internal precedent is an org-owned, org-managed client cert (HIST-106, "Issued new cert; added expiry alert") with no rotation attempt in-window. Combined with F9's error text naming OUR cert's notAfter exactly equal to onset, H2 retains no positive evidence (only UNVERIFIED F6 and one unevidenced hop) and is now properly demoted. (2) H4's rejection is no longer assertion-based: ledger-db connections_active flat (mean 62.31, 12:15 bucket 62.64), slow_queries_per_min flat-to-improving (9.02->1.11), 0 WARN+ lines; kafka messages_in_per_s flat (mean 2531.6) with under_replicated_partitions hard 0.0 across all 24 buckets, 0 api-gateway ERROR lines over an intact, non-truncated window. A shared-dependency fault is contradicted by measured health, not mere absence of change events. Temporal order is excellent (notAfter=12:15:00Z, first rejection 12:15:27Z, onset 12:15:00Z in the business metric). Scope and calibration are the residual soft spots, but neither is blocking: the alternative causes that would inflate blast radius are the same ones already contradicted, so the unchecked neighbour metrics cannot realistically re-rank H1 above another hypothesis. Two minor caveats remain non-blocking: the "impact confined to payment-service" statement rests on structural dependency edges (F1/F16, bank-partner-api's only caller) plus flat shared-component health rather than neighbour-service metric values, and the cert's issuance entity is inferred from org precedent rather than a verbatim registry record (F19) — a documented, permanently-unavailable data source, so no further query would help.

tasks.objective: Establish the true onset time and blast radius of the incident from telemetry, using 2026-04-02T12:00-14:00 window: (1) per-service error rate, latency (p50/p95/p99), throughput and timeout/retry counts for payment-service and its dependencies — look specifically for HTTP 200 responses with erroneous/degraded business status codes, long-tail latency without 5xx, and reduced request volume; (2) identify any other service whose metrics deviate in the same minute. Report whether the green payment-service HTTP error panel is a real signal or a metric blind spot, and which services show genuine anomalies.
tasks.answer: The payment-service HTTP error-rate panel is a genuine metric blind spot: HTTP error_rate stayed flat at ~0.2% (5xx only) all window, while the business-level payment_success_rate collapsed from ~99% to ~2.5% at 12:15:00Z and stayed there. The true onset is 2026-04-02T12:15:00Z (first PENDING_RETRY error 12:15:27Z; first cert-expiry error 12:16:44Z), caused by mTLS client-certificate expiry (notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z) against external bank-partner-api. It is not a client-app or bank-side problem, and impacts full payment success (not just a tail).

tasks.objective: Build the change/context timeline for 2026-04-02 11:00-14:00: list deployments and config changes for payment-service AND all upstream/downstream services and shared components (queues, DB, auth, bank/PSP connectors, feature flags, rate limits), plus the service dependency map for payment-service (who it calls, who calls it, shared components). Report what changed and when, which components are shared with other services, and any precedent fitting this signature.
tasks.answer: In 2026-04-02 11:00-14:00 there were zero deployments and exactly one config change: payment-service's bank.api.timeout_ms raised 3000→5000 ms at 11:20:00Z (author p.nair, reason \"partner advisory\"). The only deployment that day was settlement-service v1.9.0 at 10:30 (batch CSV exporter, still live). payment-service calls ledger-db (shared, also used by order/portfolio/settlement-service), bank-partner-api (external, NO telemetry) and kafka (shared); it is called by api-gateway. Given the silent-failure signature, the untraced external bank connector and the shared ledger-db/kafka (usable by neighbours) are the components to inspect; HIST-105 (bank partner API 5xx) is the closest precedent, though no historical incident actually matches 'payment failures with a green error-rate dashboard'.

tasks.objective: Using the onset time and affected-service set found in task a, correlate them against the change timeline from task b: determine whether any deploy/config change precedes the onset by a plausible interval on the affected components (not only on payment-service), and whether changes are isolated to payment-service or shared. Conclude with the most likely fault location (payment-service, a specific dependency, or external bank side) and rule in/out the client-app/bank-only theory.
tasks.answer: No deploy or config change is temporally aligned with the 12:15:00Z onset: there were zero deployments in 11:00-14:00Z (only settlement-service v1.9.0 at 10:30, off the payment path) and a single payment-service config change 55 min earlier (bank.api.timeout_ms 3000->5000 at 11:20Z). The change set is isolated to payment-service, not shared, and shared components (ledger-db, kafka) show no change correlation. The fault location is therefore the payment-service <-> external bank-partner-api mTLS boundary (client certificate expiring at exactly 12:15:00Z), not a payment-service code/config defect and not a client-app problem. The bank-only theory is ruled out as the cause: all calls failed at the client's own TLS handshake with 'our client cert ... notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z', i.e. a credential the organisation owns, though the bank endpoint is where the failure surfaces.

Conclude whether this cert is a credential the organisation owns (locking H1) or one whose trust could have been changed externally (keeping H2 alive). tasks.answer: The available records confirm the CA/credential ownership indirectly but not directly: no certificate/credential registry, secret-store entry, or renewal record for CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal was retrievable — the only internal discriminator present is HIST-106, our own prior credential_expiry incident with the resolution "Issued new cert; added expiry alert" executed by our team, and the absence of any deploy/config/rotation attempt in 12:15-14:00Z. This pattern supports the cert being an org-owned mTLS client credential whose expiry (not a bank-side trust change) is the mechanism, aligning with H1; but because no verbatim registry/ownership record exists, H2 cannot be fully excluded on the certificate record alone.

Because the shared datastore and queue are untouched at the onset minute while payment-service's own business-success metric collapsed to 2.18% at 12:15 (F8) and the only failing path is the external bank mTLS call (F9/F11), the impact is confined to the bank-partner-api mTLS path -- this empirically eliminates H4 (shared ledger/kafka damage) and validates H1's scope as payment-service's outbound bank call only. H1 (expired mTLS client cert to bank-partner-api) is the best-supported hypothesis: the true onset is tightly established at 2026-04-02T12:15:00Z (payment_success_rate 99.68%->2.18% in one minute), the diagnostic error text names OUR client cert (CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal) with notAfter exactly equal to the onset minute, 171 'tls: expired certificate' errors, bank_api_error_rate sustained 100%, and the fast-fail latency drop (330ms->140ms) explains why the HTTP 5xx panel stayed green. Alternatives H3/H4/H5 are properly contradicted (mis-timed changes, wrong failure mode, wrong layer). However, two things block an "accept": (1) H2 is ranked active at 0.15 but is NOT actually separated from H1 by evidence — both rest on the same client-side error text, and the only discriminator (is the cert internally issued/managed vs partner-provisioned/trust-changed?) has never been queried. (2) H4 was 'rejected' partly by asserting shared-component health without ever querying ledger-db/kafka metrics, and the blast-radius check across neighbours (api-gateway, order/portfolio/settlement) is unanswered — so "fault confined to payment-service's bank path" is inferred from absence of evidence rather than measured. These are obtainable and would change ranking/trust, so send back one targeted round.

Grounding: H1's chain is well grounded on F8/F9/F10/F11/F12/F18. Its two assumptions (internal cert ownership; expiry inferred only from error text) are acknowledged and are exactly the H1-vs-H2 discriminator, which is currently unresolved. H2 cites only UNVERIFIED F6 and has an unevidenced hop — but F9's "our client cert ... notAfter=..." attributed to the client side is the only evidence against it, and since bank-partner-api has no telemetry, the external view is permanently unobtainable; this may be inherently unresolvable rather than fixable.

Temporal: onset is excellently established and the proposed cause (notAfter=12:15:00Z, first rejection 12:15:27Z) precedes it by <1 min — no complaint here.

Scope: only payment-service is examined. No other service's metrics were checked at 12:15; "confined to payment-service" is an unverified claim.

Alternatives: H3/H4/H5 dismissals are sound for timing/failure-mode reasons. H4's rejection is the weakest — it relies on "no change event touches shared components," but the actual test (LEDGER-db/kafka health around 12:15, and non-bank payment paths) was never run, and a shared-component problem could also leave the bank TLS path failing if the cert is unrelated. Worth one confirming query.

Data quality: F7 (green panel) rests on 5xx alone — correctly identified as a blind spot, and F8 provides the business metric. F12 latency drop is a single strong signal, not a lone "healthy" claim. Main gap is the unqueried shared-component/neighbour telemetry and the missing cert-ownership record.

Calibration: 0.78 is too high while H2 remains unevidenced-but-not-separated and blast radius is unchecked. Cap 0.65.

challenges.issue: Chain is grounded but rests on the assumption that the cert is internally owned/renewed; there is no lifecycle record. If the cert was partner-provisioned, H2 becomes viable.

Ranked active (0.15) yet supported only by UNVERIFIED F6 and an unevidenced 'bank rotates trust at 12:15' hop. It has not been separated from H1 by any direct evidence; the discriminator (cert issuer / partner-side change) was never queried. However, bank-partner-api has_telemetry=false, so a partner-side view is likely permanently unobtainable — this may be an irreducible ambiguity rather than a fixable gap.

Rejected partly by asserting shared-component health without ever querying ledger-db/kafka metrics. 'No change event touches shared components' is not evidence of health; absence-of-evidence was used as proof.

Scope/blast-radius is unverified: no other service's metrics (api-gateway, order/portfolio/settlement) were checked at 12:15, so 'fault confined to payment-service bank path' is inferred, not measured.
Stated confidence 0.78 exceeds what the evidence separates, given H2 remains open and blast radius unchecked.

evidence_requests.question: Determine the certificate lifecycle/issuance for CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal: is it internally issued and managed by our org (mTLS client cert for outbound bank calls), or is it provisioned/trusted by bank-partner-api? Check any certificate/credential registry, secret store entries, renewal records, or config referencing this CN, and whether any renewal/rotation occurred around 12:15-14:00Z.
evidence_requests.rationale: This is the single discriminator between H1 (our expired client cert) and H2 (partner trust change). H1 currently rests on this as an acknowledged assumption; resolving it could flip or lock the ranking.

evidence_requests.question: Query ledger-db and kafka health metrics (write/read errors, latency, connection failures) and payment-service non-bank paths (ledger writes, kafka produces) around 12:00-14:00Z; confirm whether anything deviates at 12:15. Also check api-gateway, order-service, portfolio-service and settlement-service error/latency/success metrics for anomalies in the same minute.

critiques.summary: Round-1 blockers are resolved to the extent obtainable. (1) H1-vs-H2 separation: the shared-component/neighbour telemetry was actually queried, and the discriminator for H2 was pursued to its limit. F23 establishes the credential-use direction is outbound-only (bank-partner-api has no callers, shared=false, no push path), and F19/F20/F24 establish the closest internal precedent is an org-owned, org-managed client cert (HIST-106, "Issued new cert; added expiry alert") with no rotation attempt in-window. Combined with F9's error text naming OUR cert's notAfter exactly equal to onset, H2 retains no positive evidence (only UNVERIFIED F6 and one unevidenced hop) and is now properly demoted. (2) H4's rejection is no longer assertion-based: ledger-db connections_active flat (mean 62.31, 12:15 bucket 62.64), slow_queries_per_min flat-to-improving (9.02->1.11), 0 WARN+ lines; kafka messages_in_per_s flat (mean 2531.6) with under_replicated_partitions hard 0.0 across all 24 buckets, 0 api-gateway ERROR lines over an intact, non-truncated window. A shared-dependency fault is contradicted by measured health, not mere absence of change events. Temporal order is excellent (notAfter=12:15:00Z, first rejection 12:15:27Z, onset 12:15:00Z in the business metric). Scope and calibration are the residual soft spots, but neither is blocking: the alternative causes that would inflate blast radius are the same ones already contradicted, so the unchecked neighbour metrics cannot realistically re-rank H1 above another hypothesis. Two minor caveats remain non-blocking: the "impact confined to payment-service" statement rests on structural dependency edges (F1/F16, bank-partner-api's only caller) plus flat shared-component health rather than neighbour-service metric values, and the cert's issuance entity is inferred from org precedent rather than a verbatim registry record (F19) — a documented, permanently-unavailable data source, so no further query would help.

challenges.issue: Assumption 2 (CN is internally issued/managed) is inferred from org precedent HIST-106 rather than a verbatim registry/secret-store record, which F19 confirms does not exist in the toolset. Non-blocking because it is a permanently unavailable data source and all structural/directional evidence (F23) plus the matching notAfter in our own client-side error text (F9) points the same way.

The 'impact confined to payment-service's bank path' scope claim rests on structural dependency edges and flat shared-component health; the four neighbour-service metric queries (order/portfolio/settlement/api-gateway) never executed, so blast radius is unconfirmed by direct measurement.

Still has an unevidenced hop (bank-side trust change) and cites UNVERIFIED F6 as support; it is demoted on the absence of any positive evidence rather than being positively falsified, which is inherent given has_telemetry=false.

Rejected soundly, but note that ledger-db/kafka have no direct error metrics (F25/F28), so 'healthy' for these components is proxy-based (connections_active, slow_queries, messages_in_per_s, under_replicated_partitions) plus zero log lines — a multi-metric proxy, not a single-metric claim, so acceptable.
